chapter: Decca years and the First Herd
title: Bebop contacts: Dizzy writing, Charlie Parker sitting in, Kansas City tape
summary: Dizzy Gillespie wrote for the band and Charlie Parker sat in often; an afternoon Kansas City concert was taped and later released by bootleg labels.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Did you have very much communication at
the time or interest from some of the small group, revolutionary bebop groups were having? I know you had some other kinds of musicians coming in and out.
Oh, yeah. Yeah, well, Dizzy started to write for our band. He did a couple --

And then, too, I think the fact that Charlie Parker had made such a big dent into the whole jazz scene, and that we were all very conscious of this, as he, I guess, was conscious of what we were into, because he used to come over and sit in with the band, very often. And that was the reason that there was a tape, finally, from Kansas City which was a put-together date by someone, as far as a place to play together.

It was supposedly an afternoon hangout, get-together, in Kansas City for a group of people that liked Charlie and liked our band, so they thought it would be marvelous. So that's how it came about. We didn't know anyone was taping it, however.
I see. Was that just a single concert?
Yeah, that's right, just one afternoon concert.
Do you recall when that was? '46?
I think it was later, it was '47.
Do you know what's become of that tape? Did it ever appear?

Yes, yeah, sure. It's released on some label out of Europe or somewhere. I the other dav was in New York, and in our bin at Sam Goody's I had certainly far more -- I was outnumbered in releases that are bootleg products than I was by legitimate. But we were well represented in everything.
